name: SNAP (EBT)
description: Use your EBT card to buy food at markets that are SNAP-authorized. Most markets swipe your card at an information table and give you tokens to spend at stalls.
howToRedeem: Go to the market information table first. Tell them how much you want to spend; they swipe your EBT card and give you tokens. Tokens don't expire at most markets.
eligibility: Households enrolled in SNAP. Apply through the Department of Transitional Assistance (DTA).
verificationNote: Market SNAP status comes from the USDA FNS retailer list and the MDAR market layer at build time.

name: Healthy Incentives Program (HIP)
description: When you use SNAP to buy fruits and vegetables from a HIP vendor, the same amount goes back on your EBT card, up to a monthly limit based on household size.
howToRedeem: Pay with your EBT card at a HIP vendor (or the market table at HIP markets) for eligible fruits and vegetables. The refund appears on your receipt and your card right away.
eligibility: All Massachusetts SNAP households. No sign-up needed.
verificationNote: Monthly limits ($40 / $60 / $80 by household size) are the figures DTA has published since 2021. mass.gov was unreachable from the build environment on 2026-10-17, so recheck before relying on them.

name: WIC Farmers' Market Nutrition Program
description: WIC participants receive farmers' market coupons each summer to spend on fresh, locally grown fruits, vegetables and herbs.
howToRedeem: Look for a sign saying the farmer accepts WIC farmers' market coupons. Hand the coupons to the farmer; no change is given.
eligibility: WIC participants. Coupons are handed out through local WIC offices, usually starting in June.
verificationNote: Coupon amounts change each year, so we don't show a dollar figure.

name: Senior Farmers' Market Nutrition Program
description: Income-eligible older adults receive coupons to spend on fresh, locally grown produce at participating farmers.
howToRedeem: Give coupons to farmers displaying the program sign. Coupons are for fruits, vegetables and herbs only.
eligibility: Adults 60+ who meet income guidelines. Coupons are distributed through local councils on aging and elder services.
verificationNote: Coupon amounts change each year, so we don't show a dollar figure.

name: WIC Cash Value Benefit
description: Some markets report accepting the WIC fruit and vegetable cash-value benefit. We show this exactly as the source lists it.
howToRedeem: Ask the market manager before shopping. MassGIS documentation notes that WIC cash value vouchers generally aren't redeemable at Massachusetts farmers markets.
verificationNote: Shown as the source states it; call ahead.

name: Double Up Food Bucks
description: A national SNAP match run by Fair Food Network and partners: spend SNAP on fruits and vegetables and get the same amount free. Massachusetts uses HIP instead.
howToRedeem: At participating markets outside Massachusetts, visit the market table with your EBT card.

name: Boston Farmers Market Coupon Program
description: The City of Boston's Office of Food Justice has distributed farmers' market coupons through community partners. Participation varies by year.
howToRedeem: Coupons are handed out through community partners; check boston.gov for the current year's list of participating markets.
eligibility: Set each year by the City of Boston.
verificationNote: No machine-readable list of participating markets was available at build time, so no market is tagged with this program yet.
